Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is pulling together the internal ask around how the Azure private offer will be reflected in our distributor/reseller splits. Two quick clarifications we need before legal drafts anything:

1) Territory carveouts: Aureum operates in US West and US Central commercial markets with a separate state-level reseller for government contracts. How should we specify territory in the PO so that the reseller commission doesn’t inadvertently apply to gov contracts?

2) Passback schedule: Your spreadsheet referenced a monthly passback for partner margins. We need to confirm whether the passback is calculated off list price or net revenue after AWS marketplace fees.

Can Ben or someone on your team share the canonical wording you expect in the private offer and any sample line-item we can paste into our SOW?

Laura — great questions. Short answers up front, details below and attaching a draft private-offer PDF & a simple commission workbook for the partner team.

1) Territory carveouts: We recommend explicitly enumerating SKUs and AZ regions in the private offer (e.g. az-west-2 commercial SKUs only) and adding an exclusion line for any gov-oriented reseller IDs. That prevents the marketplace from routing gov purchases to the same passback rule.

2) Passback basis: Passbacks are normally calculated on the net revenue we receive from the cloud marketplace after platform fees. That means list price minus AWS marketplace fee (the Marketplace fee line shows in the invoice). We can do an alternative definition if Aureum prefers passback on list price, but that will change the effective partner margin — I've shown both scenarios in the attached commission-split.xlsx.

Sample private-offer clause (suggested):
"Partner passback and territory. The Seller (Redwood Inference) shall apply partner passback to transactions for the specified commercial SKUs in regions [AZ-WEST-2, AZ-CENTRAL-1]. Government or public-sector purchases sold under distinct reseller agreements are excluded from this passback. Passback shall be calculated on the Net Marketplace Revenue (gross list price less Marketplace Fee and applicable taxes) and paid monthly to the partner as outlined in the attached schedule."

Next step: Ben — can you review the clause for tax/treatment implications? Irene — can you confirm whether our private-offer flow supports SKU-level region scoping for Azure?

Best,

Looping in my notes for legal/finance. TL;DR: clause looks fine but watch two edge cases: taxes and reseller refunds.

- Taxes: If Aureum is in a tax jurisdiction that requires marketplace to remit tax, the net revenue can swing. We recommend adding a sentence that passback is calculated after any taxes remitted by the marketplace.

- Refunds/chargebacks: If a customer refund occurs within the settlement period, the partner passback should be netted on next month's statement. That prevents overpayments.

Irene — on SKU scoping: Azure private offers allow SKU scoping to a degree (you can constrain by offer alias and plan), but region-scoped enforcement is limited in the UI. Practically we scope by offer id and then rely on reseller rules + marketplace filters. If Aureum needs hard region enforcement, engineering may need to add a tag-based rule and ops will have to enforce in billing. That is doable but will add ~2 weeks to implementation.

Example line to add: "Passback amount will be adjusted for any taxes and marketplace remittances; any refunds within the settlement period will be deducted from subsequent passback payments."

I'll prepare a short note for Finance and Legal to include with the PO.

- Ben

• For refunds: Aureum requests a 90-day lookback window for chargebacks to be netted against passback rather than month-to-month reconciliation. Would that be acceptable?

If we can get an updated draft clause with the tax language and the 90-day lookback sentence, procurement will hand the doc to legal today. If ops will need to tag-based enforce regions and that adds two weeks, please confirm the timeline now so we can align our rollout plan.
